descriptor.scene:
A PORTRAIT BOOK COVER, vertical. Looking into the ordinary working room in warm daylight, the makers at work in loose clusters, nobody centred or leading. Lived-in and unremarkable and warm. Compose the people and desks in the LOWER TWO THIRDS and leave the UPPER THIRD relatively calm and uncluttered, because the title goes there.

BAKED TITLE LETTERING, hand-painted directly into the artwork in the upper third, in large warm off-white capitals, well clear of every face. It must read EXACTLY, spelled correctly and completely:
THE ROOM IT WAS MADE IN

Directly beneath it, in much smaller capitals of the same hand, spelled EXACTLY:
A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story

Those two lines are the ONLY text anywhere in the image.
descriptor.negatives: NO logos, NO company marks, NO branding, NO slogans on walls, NO invented signage, NO readable words on any screen, whiteboard, notebook or page in the scene. THE TWO TITLE STRINGS BELOW ARE REQUIRED DESIGNED ELEMENTS AND MUST BE RENDERED, prominently and spelled exactly. They are the only text permitted in this image. NO single figure centred, elevated or spotlit as a leader. NO caricature of any identifiable real person or company. NO soaring ceilings, atriums or glass boxes. NO dramatic lighting.

prompt:
Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. WARM EDITORIAL INK-AND-WASH illustration: soft illustrative linework, warm restrained colour, gentle washes, the look of a thoughtful printed picture book for adults. NOT neon, NOT 3D or CGI or Pixar, NOT glossy plastic, NOT neo-comic, NO HUD or arc-reactor vocabulary. ONE single full-bleed scene per image: never a grid of panels, never a contact sheet. This book argues that a made thing comes out like the room it was made in, so the room must always look ORDINARY and lived-in rather than impressive, and each spread is set wherever its own scene description says.
